children: Brokerages turned more bullish on Paytm and Pine Labs shares after the introduction of MDR on select UPI merchant payments. The levy opened a new revenue stream for payment companies, prompting analysts to raise earnings estimates and target prices. Paytm gained 2.6 percent to Rs 1,775 on September 16, while Pine Labs fell 6 percent to Rs 182.2 despite target prices that imply more than 25 percent upside from current levels.

Emkay maintained 'Buy' ratings on both stocks, raising its Paytm target price to Rs 2,400 from Rs 1,700 and Pine Labs' to Rs 230 from Rs 190. The revised targets imply upside of about 35 percent and 26 percent, respectively, from Wednesday's prices. The brokerage estimates the new MDR revenue stream adds Rs 678 per share to Paytm's valuation and about Rs 43 per share to Pine Labs.
Jefferies raised its target price on Paytm to Rs 2,150 and on Pine Labs to Rs 235. JM Financial also lifted its Paytm target to Rs 2,150 from Rs 1,950 while retaining a 'Buy' rating.

For Paytm, Emkay estimates UPI MDR revenue of Rs 11.2 billion in FY28, assuming a realised take rate of 10 basis points. JM Financial expects incremental revenue of Rs 2.1 billion in FY27 and Rs 4.7 billion in FY28, with incremental adjusted EBITDA reaching Rs 4.4 billion in FY28. Goldman Sachs said the MDR framework could lift its FY28 Paytm EBITDA estimate by 40-70 percent in a high-end scenario.

For Pine Labs, Emkay estimates Rs 1.55 billion of UPI MDR revenue in FY28, based on a realised take rate of 6 basis points. The brokerage expects the additional revenue to accrue on payment infrastructure and merchant relationships that are already in place.

The market reaction was nevertheless mixed. Paytm, which has gained 37.5 percent so far in 2026 against an 11.2 percent fall in the Nifty 50, traded higher at Rs 1,775. Pine Labs dropped 6 percent to Rs 182.2 and is down 22.5 percent year-to-date. Mobikwik, for which no brokerage target was readily available, reversed early gains to trade 1.3 percent lower at Rs 198.3, taking its year-to-date decline to 13.8 percent.

The brokerage optimism follows NPCI's introduction of a 0.4 percent MDR on eligible UPI person-to-merchant transactions above Rs 2,000 from October 15. Several exemptions and lower rates apply, meaning the eventual earnings benefit will depend on each company's eligible transaction mix and the share of MDR it retains. Emkay said the broader significance is that UPI acquiring now has a recurring, transaction-linked commercial revenue model rather than relying on an annual subsidy.

title: Paytm, Pine Labs stocks get bullish brokerage calls after UPI MDR; targets imply up to 35% upside
